The fixed circuit ran on garnet:mock with 100 shots. Job 01a15f17-b378-73d2-bfeb-daeabd118ec2 completed with counts {"00": 46, "11": 54}. The mock returns random results, so these counts do not prove the circuit makes entanglement on hardware. The circuit itself is the standard Bell construction from the IQM docs.

I made two changes.

1. The original circuit used QB25. Garnet has only QB1 to QB20. I replaced QB25 with QB2. The live garnet:mock calibration lists only two cz couplers that touch QB1: QB1-QB2 and QB1-QB4.

2. The original circuit used "cx". That is not a native IQM operation. Garnet accepts prx, cz, and measure, plus a few others. "cx" is not one of them. I built the CNOT from native gates. Ry(pi/2) on QB2 and a CZ on QB1-QB2 come first. Then I apply Ry(-pi/2) on QB2. Each Ry is a prx with phase pi/2. QB1 keeps the original Ry(pi/2), which is prx angle pi/2, phase pi/2.

The fixed circuit is: prx(QB1, pi/2, pi/2), prx(QB2, pi/2, pi/2), cz(QB1, QB2), prx(QB2, -pi/2, pi/2), then measure(QB1, QB2) with key "m". The ideal state is (|00> - |11>)/sqrt(2). Both qubits are measured.

Before submitting, I checked the circuit with create_run_request against the live calibration. I submitted one job only. The script is /Users/claytonchancey/Desktop/quantum/.claude/worktrees/wf_1a6926f8-f6c-39/scratch/bell_fix.py.
